t6136.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān al-Madanī as truthful, except that the ḥadīths of Abū Hurayra became confused for him. He belongs to the fifth generation and died in the year forty-eight.
as: صدوق إلا أنه اختلطت عليه أحاديث أبي هريرة
Truthful, except that the ḥadīths of Abū Hurayra became confused for him
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
جميعا ثقة، وما أقربهما، كان ابن عيينة يثني على محمد بن عجلان.
Both he and Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah were trustworthy and close in standing. Ibn ʿUyaynah praised Ibn ʿAjlān.
حدثنا محمد بن عجلان، وكان ثقة.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān narrated to us and was trustworthy.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
محمد بن عجلان ثقة أوثق من محمد بن عمرو بن علقمة، ما يشك في هذا أحد
Ibn ʿAjlān was trustworthy, more trustworthy than Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah, and no one doubted it.
داود بن قيس, quoted by al-Mizzī
إنها اختلطت على ابن عجلان يعني في حديث سعيد المقبري
The material from Saʿīd al-Maqburī became confused for Ibn ʿAjlān.

t7319.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hammām ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAwdhī al-Baṣrī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh or Abū Bakr, as trustworthy though sometimes erring, of the seventh generation, who died in 64 or 65.
as: يزيد بن هارون, quoted by al-Mizzī
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
همام ثقة، وهو أثبت من أبان في يحيى بن أبي كثير
Hammām is reliable and more precise than Abān in reporting from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr.
همام عندي في الصدق مثل ابن أبي عروبة
I consider Hammām equal to Ibn Abī ʿArūbah in truthfulness.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة، صالح، وهو في قتادة أحب إلي من حماد بن سلمة، وأحسنهم حديثا عن قتادة
Reliable and acceptable. I prefer him to Ḥammād ibn Salamah for Qatādah and consider his hadith from Qatādah the best of them.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ولم يكن همام عندي بدون القوم في قتادة، ولم يكن ليحيى فيه رأي، وكان عبد الرحمن ابن مهدي حسن الرأي فيه
I ranked Hammām alongside the others in Qatādah. Yaḥyā did not think well of him, while Ibn Mahdī did.
يزيد بن زريع, quoted by al-Mizzī
Hammām’s memory is poor, and his book is sound.
كان ثقة، ربما غلط في الحديث
He was reliable and sometimes made errors in hadith.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
There is nothing objectionable about him.
عفان بن مسلم, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان يحيى بن سعيد يعترض على همام في كثير من حديثه، فلما قدم معاذ بن هشام نظرنا في كتبه فوجدناه يوافق هماما في كثير مما كان يحيى ينكره، فكف يحيى بعد عنه
Yaḥyā objected to much of Hammām’s hadith. Muʿādh’s books agreed with many of the reports Yaḥyā objected to, and Yaḥyā then held back.
عبد الله بن المبارك, quoted by al-Mizzī
Hammām is precise in transmitting from Qatādah.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Hammām is firm in all his shaykhs.
محمد بن عبد الله بن عمار الموصلي, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان يحيى بن سعيد لا يعبأ بهمام
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd paid no heed to Hammām.
وهمام أشهر وأصدق من أن يذكر له حديث، وأحاديثه مستقيمة عن قتادة
Hammām is too well known and truthful to have a hadith cited against him; his hadiths from Qatādah are sound.
وكان ثقة ربما غلط في الحديث.
Reliable, though he sometimes erred in hadith.

t8196.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū ʿĀṣim al-Ghanawī as maqbūl (acceptable) and of the fifth generation.

t8233.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū ʿUbayda ibn ʿUqba ibn Nāfiʿ al-Fihrī, said to be named Murra, as acceptable (maqbūl) and of the third generation. He died in 107 AH; Muslim and al-Nasāʾī cite him.
as: He is acceptable (i.e., his reports are accepted when corroborated).
stu: Named next to each other in two or more indexed chains

t8318.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Kabbāsh al-Sulamī or al-ʿAbsī; it is said he is Abū ʿAyyāsh and Abū Kabbāsh is a nickname. He is unknown, of the third generation, cited by al-Tirmidhī.

t8387.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Abū al-Mughīra, who transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās a report censuring innovation, as unknown and of the fourth generation. Ibn Mājah transmits from him.

t8400.bio: Ibn Ḥajar names Abū Mūsā al-Ḥaddhāʾ al-Makkī as Ṣuhayb, acceptable, of the fourth generation; some say there are two persons.

t8475.bio: Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr transmits from his father; he is not known and is not named, of the fifth generation.
as: He is not known and is not named.

t8509.bio: Ibn Ḥajar notes that Zahrah ibn Maʿbad, of the second generation, transmits from an unnamed paternal cousin, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir.

t910.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jurhad ibn Rizāḥ al-Aslamī, a Medinan Companion, one of the people of the Ṣuffah; he is said to have died in 61 AH.
